evidence: Inventory: 2 gate criteria, 43 functional binary criteria (total weight 58.5), 5 polish binary, 5 visual likert. Strengths: nearly every functional/polish criterion names a concrete browser outcome with a distinctive, durable probe: per-review suffixed jobs J1/J2 and named cards A-F, V-Z, A2 (functional prompt.md:15,27); seeded order and Noor's seeded note re-read across restart_app (judge.toml hro_restart, prompt.md:25,51); independent-context readbacks for job/candidate/reorder (hro_job_open, hro_add_candidate, hro_reorder); every refusal row requires 'nothing changes' plus a same-kind control, and line 17 requires a fresh board read with current version before each rule/role replay so a stale-version refusal cannot masquerade as a rule refusal; replays use captured real requests only; focus/scroll/draft legs are read via document.activeElement/getBoundingClientRect/scroll offsets (hro_refused_put_back, hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_earlier_place); live rows use a fixed 15 s window with 'first snapshot at or after 15 s'. No criterion asks for a source read; the status-code assertion in hro_anonymous ('refused with 401') is paired with 'return no workspace data; nothing changes' and is a public rule (hireops_rules.md:21). Gate render/constraints are concrete (wrong password stays signed out; UI-created job+card seen in a new context as Observer). DEFECT (every instance): order/placement outcomes are graded only on the mover's own page, with no durable readback, although the public requirement is a server-held order 'the same for everyone' that 'survives a reload' (hireops_rules.md:57-59, instruction.md:3) and moves are optimistic by rule ('A move appears on the mover's board immediately', hireops_rules.md:84). Instances: (1) hro_arrive_bottom (w1): 'B, moved into a Screen that already holds A, lands below A; A ... then lands below B' - no reload/independent read in criterion or protocol M (prompt.md:29). (2) hro_bulk_move (w1.5): 'arrive at the bottom of that stage in board order (Y, W, X ...)' and 'A2, V' - read on Rafael's page only (prompt.md:35 steps 4, 13). (3) hro_undo_restores (w2): 'puts Y, W and X back in Applied at their places (Y, W, X, Z, A2)' - mover's page only (step 5). Contrast hro_reorder and hro_add_candidate, which explicitly require 'an independent context sees the same order'. The golden itself computes arrival placement client-side first (solution/app/public/js/board.js:172-186 localMove + renderBoard before the POST), so the probed observable can be produced without the server. Notes (not counted as the Fail): (a) hro_thread_access accepts Ingrid's foreign-manager read isolation as 'not listed' with no read replay (protocol T, prompt.md:39 'check it is not available or refused'; only send replays are mandated) - a hidden-UI observation, mainly a coverage/negative-control concern for rows 26/30. (b) hro_candidate_private's rejection-reason/rejected-from probe relies on Tomas's judge-made rejection while his page is open; Lena Fischer's seeded rejected card (APP-301, reason 'Portfolio did not show shipped product work.', rejected_from SCREEN, note 'Portfolio is concept work only.') would be a stronger durable distinctive probe but K only signs in Noor and Tomas (prompt.md:43); Noor's seeded note still gives a distinctive notes probe. (c) Visual likert rows are craft judgements with five anchors and named surfaces; acceptable for the visual dimension per SKILL.md likert note. (d) hro_add_candidate/hro_job_open 'shown wherever the app shows' legs are conditional but decidable; team is independently required in hro_candidate_view. Runtime: raw-evidence-index hashes verified; it is scripted golden evidence only, no configured judge run exists, so how the judge actually reads order after optimistic moves is unmeasured.
counterexample: A submission renders moves optimistically by appending the card(s) to the bottom of the target column in client state (like the golden's localMove) but its server move/bulk/undo endpoints store the wrong position (e.g. position stays at the source index, or arrivals are inserted at position 0, or bulk sets keep selection order), and it only reconciles from the server on its 10-second poll. The judge reads Rafael's page right after each action, as protocols M and B direct, sees B below A, Y/W/X in board order and Y,W,X,Z,A2 after undo, and awards hro_arrive_bottom, hro_bulk_move and hro_undo_restores (4.5 of 58.5 functional weight), although every other person and every reload sees a different order, violating 'the same for everyone'. Conversely nothing here wrongly fails a conforming app.
suggested_fix: Add to hro_arrive_bottom, hro_bulk_move and hro_undo_restores (and their protocol steps in M and B) that the stated order must also be what a fresh read in an independent context of another recruiter (or a reload after the action settles) shows, mirroring hro_reorder's existing wording.
